introH2: 🏙️ What kinds of great-vibe hotels does Phrae have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Phrae is an up-and-coming secondary city, and more young travellers drive or fly up every year to wander the old town, visit temples, eat local food, and photograph the teak-wood houses. The places to stay here come in more shapes than many people expect — some are Lanna garden boutiques with a swimming pool right in the old-town district, some are bare-concrete lofts on the Yom River within walking distance of the night-market street, some are small B&Bs run hands-on by the owners that feel like staying with relatives, and some are edge-of-town budget stays that are easy to drive to and the lightest on the wallet. Plenty of first-timers in Phrae end up picking a stay that doesn't match their style, then waste time travelling in and out of town even though the sights are clustered close together. This article rounds up 10 Phrae hotels and stays we've reviewed in depth — in the old town, along the Yom River, and on the edge of town — all drawn from reading real guest reviews, telling you the upsides and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites, with direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Phrae is a small city with no mass-transit rail, and the main sights cluster in the old town inside the earthen walls, easy to explore on foot or by bicycle. There are three ways to reach Phrae: by air, landing at Phrae Airport (PRH), which is only about a 5–10 min drive from town, with daily flights from Bangkok; by coach, arriving at Phrae's provincial bus terminal near the city centre; or by car — about 6–7 hours from Bangkok, about 3 hours from Chiang Mai. Several hotels in this article offer free airport and bus-terminal transfers, handy if you're not driving yourself. The areas covered here: Nai Wiang — the heart of the old town, walking distance to Khum Chao Luang, Baan Wongburi, temples, and markets; Yom Riverside — quiet and calm, near the Saturday Kad Kong Kao walking street; Pa Maet and the edge of town — easy to drive, light on the wallet, about a 10 min drive into the centre. As for Wat Phra That Cho Hae, the city's guardian temple, it's about a 15 min drive out of town from anywhere.

entries.name: Huern Na Na Boutique Hotel
entries.badge: 🏊 Boutique with a pool, in the old town
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nai Wiang · near Khum Chao Luang, about a 5 min drive to the old town
entries.addr: 7/9 Sasibut Road, Nai Wiang, Mueang Phrae District
entries.storyHtml: We open the list of 10 Phrae hotels with a pick that suits anyone after a genuinely quiet atmosphere right in the centre of town — Huern Na Na Boutique Hotel is a 28-room boutique in the Nai Wiang area, the heart of Phrae city. The building is a contemporary Thai house with big shade trees all around, and it's about a 5 min drive into the old quarter and Khum Chao Luang. The thing real reviews mention most consistently is the calm, private Lanna garden-house feel — many guests say it feels more like staying at a relative's house than a hotel, and the staff are lovely and polite, check-in is quick, and they're good at recommending places to eat and visit. The highlight guests praise most is the outdoor saltwater pool set among green gardens — clear water, quiet, easy to swim in without jostling for space — and the saltwater system is gentler on skin and eyes than a typical chlorine pool, so it suits families with young kids. The place also throws in more freebies than you'd expect at this price: free bikes to ride around the old town, free parking, EV charging, and free transfers to Phrae Airport and the bus terminal, just give them your arrival time when you book. That makes it very easy for anyone not driving themselves. The entry-level rooms are Deluxe at around 36 sq m, while anyone wanting more space or celebrating a special occasion can take a Victoria or Empire suite at around 72 sq m, roughly double the size. Honest caveats from the reviews: the building and some rooms are showing their age, a few rooms look worn or dusty and could use more thorough cleaning, the air-con in some rooms doesn't run at full strength, and breakfast is on the simple side. So the 7.4 score reflects that this is a budget-friendly in-town boutique built around atmosphere, location, and the pool rather than brand-new rooms. But set your expectations right, pick a good room, and check the latest photos before booking, and it's genuinely good value for an in-town hotel with a pool.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want a bigger room or you're celebrating a special occasion, go for the Victoria or Empire suite (around 72 sq m). Check the latest photos and reviews of the exact room type you're booking, because condition varies room to room, and if you're arriving by plane or coach, don't forget to give your arrival time in advance to use the free transfer.

entries.storyHtml: If Huern Na Na is a small garden house, PhoomThai Garden Hotel is the larger version — a 46-room garden hotel in the Nai Wiang area that many people call an oasis in the middle of Phrae. What sets it apart from the usual in-town stays is that it has a real garden, not a converted shophouse — the three-storey building is laid out in an L shape wrapped around a green garden that deliberately kept the original trees, with ferns, orchids, and big shade trees. Teak woodwork in the rooms and common areas gives the whole place a warm, distinctly northern feel. It's about a 10 min walk from the hotel to the old town, passing Wat Phra Bat Ming Muang, Khum Chao Luang, and Baan Wongburi. The thing guests praise most often and most consistently in real reviews is the caring, friendly staff — several platforms rate service as the highest-scoring category, and international guests have written that staff will help with anything to keep things smooth. Another highlight is the outdoor pool in the garden, shaded and surrounded by trees, which families with kids love, plus a spa and sauna for a relaxing massage all in one place. The food gets plenty of praise too, especially the breakfast buffet with Thai, northern, and Western options — many reviews say it's more varied than expected for a mid-sized hotel in a secondary city. For anyone without a car it's especially convenient, with a free airport transfer, free bikes, and the hotel's tuk-tuk into the old town. Honest things to bear in mind: some rooms and decor are showing their age and look dated and could use a renovation, cleanliness is inconsistent in a few rooms, and the most important thing to know is that on some nights karaoke from the bar carries up to the rooms — light sleepers should request a room away from the bar when booking. The 8.1 score from over a thousand reviews is steady and trustworthy, suited to people who prioritise the garden setting, service, and central location over brand-new rooms.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Don't miss the breakfast buffet, especially the northern dishes guests keep recommending. If you're a light sleeper, request a room away from the karaoke bar when booking, and make the most of the free airport transfer and the tuk-tuk into the old town if you're not driving.

entries.storyHtml: Ask which name comes up most often when someone's after a good place to stay in the heart of Phrae, and the answer from real reviews is Hug Inn Phrae — a small boutique B&B with just 12 rooms, opened in 2018 in the Nai Wiang area, in the old town on Thetsaban 2 Road, and the hotel with the highest score in this list at 9.2 on Trip.com (8.7 on Booking). Its number-one appeal is a location where you can walk out for a bowl of noodles, browse the market, or visit a temple in minutes without driving and hunting for parking — the old-town market is about 500 m away, and you can comfortably bike to Khum Chao Luang, Baan Wongburi, and the city's cafes on the free bikes in a single day. The thing reviews mention after the location is the design — an industrial loft style with bare-concrete walls mixed with Phrae's hand-dyed mor hom indigo and cram fabrics. Many people say it photographs beautifully from every angle, more like staying in a boutique cafe than a hotel. The standout score is its cleanliness, which many people rate a perfect 10 (Trip.com cleanliness 9.6), with comfortable beds, good hot-water pressure, and a thoughtfully prepared breakfast that isn't a mass-produced buffet, plus fresh coffee from the in-house cafe. What sets Hug Inn apart from a chain hotel is the people — the young owners look after guests hands-on and attentively, recommending places to eat and visit until many feel like they're staying with relatives and end their reviews saying they'll be back. Honest caveats: it's a small place with no pool and no lift, some rooms involve fairly steep stairs, it has only 12 rooms so it fills up fast during festivals, and there are occasional comments about a little dust on floors or sofas that the team quickly sorts out when told. If your trip is about soaking up Phrae's old town, visiting temples, eating well, and staying somewhere that feels like home, Hug Inn fits that intent almost exactly.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With only 12 rooms it fills up very fast, so book ahead and lock in a free-cancellation rate first. If you're travelling with older relatives, request a ground-floor room since there's no lift, and don't forget to ask the owners to recommend noodle shops and local cafes, which are often better than anything you'll find online.

entries.name: Taris Art Hotel Phrae
entries.revCount: Real reviews 8.2 · 92 reviews · budget, walk to Pratu Chai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nai Wiang city centre · walk to Pratu Chai and markets
entries.addr: 69 Ratchadamnoen Road, Nai Wiang, Mueang Phrae District
entries.storyHtml: Now to a pick that suits a tight budget while still keeping you in the centre of town — Taris Art Hotel Phrae is a 2-star budget hotel with 99 rooms on Ratchadamnoen Road in the Nai Wiang area of Phrae, decorated in a light art style that makes it look brighter than the usual budget hotel. The clear selling point is a starting price among the lightest of the in-town group, with Deluxe Twin rooms from only about ฿650/night, plus a location that's a roughly 5 min walk to Pratu Chai, the old city walls, and Pratu Chai market, near the Pung Thao Kong shrine, and about a 5 min drive to Khum Chao Luang. From real reviews the score is 8.2 from 92 reviews, which is very good for a hotel at this price. Most guests weigh the value and central location above all, and many say they got a clean-enough room at a price that's hard to find — ideal for travellers who just want a clean bed in a good spot and spend most of their time out exploring the old town. Rooms range from Deluxe Twin with two single beds, to a roomier Superior, up to a Junior Suite with extra sitting space for a small family. Every room has air-con, a fridge, a kettle, a TV, and a private bathroom. Honest caveats, budget-hotel style: this isn't a place with a pool or pretty gardens, the facilities are basic, and luxury isn't something to expect at this price. But if you're coming to Phrae to walk the old town, visit temples, and save your accommodation budget for food and souvenirs, Taris Art does its job — a clean bed in a good spot at a light price — and it's genuinely good value.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Prices rise over long weekends and festivals (Deluxe around ฿850) and rooms fill up fast, so booking ahead pays off. Set your expectations around value and location, and use the hotel as a base to explore Pratu Chai and the market just 5 min away.

entries.addr: 181/6 Yantrakitkoson Road, Nai Wiang, Mueang Phrae District
entries.storyHtml: Maeyom Palace Hotel is a large 104-room 3-star hotel that's been part of Phrae for a long time, and its standout feature is a location that suits one group of travellers exactly — the hotel sits across from Phrae's provincial bus terminal, just across the street on Yantrakitkoson Road, near the city centre. For anyone arriving by coach who doesn't want to find onward transport, this is convenience you won't get elsewhere on this list — just wheel your bags across the road and check in. From real reviews the score is 8.0 from as many as 644 reviews, a large sample that makes the score trustworthy, with guests split between tourists and people travelling in for business. What sets it apart from a budget hotel is that it's a large property with a pool, meeting rooms, and banquet space, catering to families, tour groups, and conferences. Rooms range from Standard Twin and Standard Double with all the basic amenities, up to a roomier Deluxe Room with a king bed, and some rooms look out over the city or the mountains. The location is also about a 7–10 min drive to Wat Chom Sawan, Pratu Chai, Khum Chao Luang, and Baan Wongburi, and about 15 min to Wat Phra That Cho Hae. Honest caveats: it's a hotel that's been open a long time, so the decor and some rooms are fairly classic and showing their age, not a brand-new modern boutique, and anyone looking for stylish design may find it a bit dated. But if you weigh the location next to the bus terminal, the convenience for people without a car, the pool, and the systematic service of a large hotel, Maeyom Palace is still a well-rounded, good-value choice in Phrae.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you arrive by coach at the provincial bus terminal, this is the most comfortable choice since it's just across the street. Prices rise over long weekends (Deluxe around ฿1,250), so book ahead, and if you want a room with a city or mountain view, ask for it when booking.

entries.name: Must Come Boutique Hotel
entries.revCount: Real reviews 7.8 · 40 reviews · small budget-friendly boutique
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Baan Nam Khong · Rong So Road · Phrae city
entries.addr: 18 Soi 2, Rong So Road, Baan Nam Khong, Phrae city
entries.storyHtml: Must Come Boutique Hotel is a small boutique hotel of about 20 rooms in the Baan Nam Khong area on Rong So Road in Phrae, suited to anyone after a simple, clean place at a light price without needing luxury. The location is a little off the old-town axis but still within the city, a 400–500 m walk to Wat Rong So and Wat Si Bun Rueang, near the Pung Thao Kong shrine, and about a 5–10 min drive to Khum Chao Luang and Kad Kong Kao. From real reviews the score is 7.8 from 40 reviews, with most guests praising the clean rooms, friendly staff, and easy-to-reach price. It's a quiet sort of stay that suits solo travellers, couples, or anyone driving to Phrae who wants a clean bed on a budget. There are several room types, from a Single Room for one person, to Twin and Double for couples, up to a Double Room with Balcony with a sitting balcony for a more open feel. Every room has air-con, a fridge, and free Wi-Fi. A handy point is the on-site parking, good for anyone driving themselves, and some listings note an airport transfer from the nearby airport. Honest caveats: it's a small boutique with basic facilities, no pool, no large in-house restaurant, and the location isn't in the heart of the old town within walking distance of everything — without a car you may need to call a ride into town now and then. But measured on cleanliness, friendliness, and a price starting at just ฿700/night, Must Come is a small boutique that's good value and easy on the mind for a budget trip to Phrae.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want a more open feel, go for the Double Room with Balcony with its sitting balcony. This place suits drivers since parking is easy and the location is a little off the old-town axis, and if you don't have a car, ask about an airport transfer when booking.

entries.addr: 3 Mueang Hit Road, Nai Wiang, Mueang Phrae District
entries.storyHtml: Phrae Nakara Hotel is a large 139-room city hotel on Mueang Hit Road in the Nai Wiang area, positioned as both a tourist hotel and Phrae's conference and banquet centre, and it scores well at 8.7 from 103 real reviews, which is high for a large hotel in a secondary city. Its strength is being a large hotel with systematic service in a central old-town location — about a 400 m walk to Phrae's street art, about 500 m to the Pung Thao Kong shrine, and within walking distance of the Saturday-evening Kad Kong Kao walking street — making it easy to use as a base for exploring the old town. Something many people like is that the hotel has renovated a new wing into Boutique Rooms with fresher decor than the original Standard rooms, so you get both a light-priced option and an updated one in the same place. Entry-level rooms are Standard at around 27 sq m with a king bed, stepping up to Boutique Room and Boutique Twin in the newly decorated wing, and up to a Family Suite of around 57 sq m for families or groups. There's a free airport transfer — Phrae Airport is about a 10 min drive — and Wat Phra Bat Ming Muang is about a 15 min walk. Honest caveats: because it's a large hotel that's been open a long time, the Standard rooms in the original wing look more classic and aged than the renovated Boutique rooms, so anyone serious about newness should choose the Boutique wing, and during conferences or banquets the common areas can be livelier than usual. But for anyone wanting a large hotel with systematic service, a location good for exploring the old town, and rooms across several price tiers, Phrae Nakara is a well-rounded, good-scoring choice in Phrae.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're serious about how new the room feels, choose the Boutique Room wing, which is more freshly decorated than the original Standard. Come on a Saturday evening to walk to the Kad Kong Kao walking street, and make the most of the free airport transfer if you're flying in.

entries.addr: 7 Chetawan Road Soi 1, Nai Wiang, Mueang Phrae District
entries.storyHtml: Come Moon Loft Hotel is a small 15-room loft-style boutique hotel on the Yom River in Phrae, scoring well at 8.7 from 37 real reviews, with a light starting price of just ฿650/night that's great value for this level of design. What sets it apart from the other stays on the list is its bare-concrete loft style in a cool, raw palette that looks modern and photographs well, plus a quiet location on the Yom River with a riverside park for a stroll about 3 min away and Wat Phra Non about a 4 min walk. Importantly, it's still about a 10 min walk to the Saturday-evening Kad Kong Kao walking street, so you get both riverside quiet and easy access to exploring the old quarter in one spot. From real reviews, guests weigh the stylish design, cleanliness, the quiet riverside location, and the easy-to-reach price — suited to couples, laid-back travellers who like a cool atmosphere, and anyone after a nicely designed room on a budget. There are two main room types: Standard Double with one large bed and Standard Twin with two beds, around 20 sq m, all with air-con, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, and a minibar. Honest caveats: it's a small place with only 15 rooms and just two room types, and at around 20 sq m the rooms are compact, not ideal for anyone wanting a big room or travelling in a larger group, and the facilities are basic with no pool. But for anyone who likes loft design, a quiet riverside location that still lets you explore the old town, and a light price, Come Moon Loft is one of the most distinctive and best-value picks in Phrae.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Come on a Saturday evening so you can walk to the Kad Kong Kao walking street from the hotel. In the morning, take a stroll in the Yom riverside park just 3 min away, and book ahead since there are only 15 rooms and it fills up fast on holidays.

entries.storyHtml: Baan I Inspire is a 22-room boutique B&B in the Nai Wiang area of Phrae, known for design that uses teak and local materials, and it scores as high as 8.9 from real reviews — though the review count is still small (15 reviews), the feedback runs fairly consistently positive. What makes it interesting is the boutique-house atmosphere with deliberate design work — using teak, the material Phrae is known for, mixed with local decor, giving the rooms a warm, tasteful contemporary-northern feel, and many reviews praise the rooms as pretty and clean. The location is on Rat Uthit Road in Nai Wiang, only about 1.3 km, or a 5 min drive, from Phrae Airport, ideal for anyone who flies in and wants to reach their stay quickly, and it's about a 5–7 min drive to Khum Chao Luang, Baan Wongburi, Wat Phong Sunan, and Kad Kong Kao. Rooms come in several sizes, from an S Room of around 24 sq m with an extra daybed, to an M Room of around 38 sq m that's more open with a teak work desk, up to an L Room, a one-bedroom suite with a separate sitting room of around 47 sq m, good for families. Honest caveats: the starting price here is higher than many on the list (from about ฿1,015/night), reflecting a focus on the group willing to pay more for design and newness, and the still-small review count means the overall picture isn't as settled as hotels with hundreds of reviews — it's a small place where the facilities lean towards a B&B rather than full amenities. But if you weigh nicely designed teak rooms, cleanliness, and a location near the airport, Baan I Inspire is a good-scoring boutique with a character of its own in Phrae.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you fly into Phrae Airport, this one is very quick to reach since it's only about a 5 min drive away. If you want an open room with a work desk, choose the M Room, and for families choose the L Room with its separate sitting room, and check the photos of each room type before booking since the sizes differ noticeably.

entries.addr: 224 Moo 7, Phaya Phon Road, Pa Maet, Mueang Phrae District
entries.storyHtml: We close out the 10 Phrae hotels with the lightest-priced pick on the list — B2 Phrae Boutique & Budget Hotel is a budget hotel in the B2 chain that many people know well for new, clean rooms at a budget price, with 78 rooms in the Pa Maet area on the edge of Phrae on Phaya Phon Road, with a starting price of just ฿590/night, the cheapest in this list. The strength of the B2 chain is consistency — you know that when you book you'll get a clean room, a usable bed, and all the basic amenities at a predictable price, and the real score confirms it at 8.6 from as many as 596 reviews, a large sample that makes the score trustworthy. This place mainly suits people who drive to Phrae, because the edge-of-town location means easy, spacious parking, and it's about a 10 min drive into the Nai Wiang town centre, about 15 min to Wat Phra That Cho Hae, and about 12 min to Khum Chao Luang and Baan Wongburi. Rooms range from a Superior of around 21 sq m with a double or twin beds, a Deluxe with a king bed and a work desk, up to a Junior Suite of around 30 sq m with a sitting corner, good for a small family. Every room has air-con, a TV, a fridge, drinking water, and hot water. Honest caveats: this is a budget hotel that's not in the heart of the old town — the edge-of-town location makes getting into town less convenient for those without a car than an in-town hotel, and it's a budget chain focused on clean simplicity, with no pool, garden, or stylish boutique design. But if you're driving yourself and want a new, clean room with predictable quality at the lightest price in town, B2 Phrae is the most good-value, easy-on-the-mind choice for a budget trip to Phrae.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: This one suits drivers because of the edge-of-town location and spacious parking — if you don't have a car, budget for the roughly 10 min ride into town. Book ahead over long weekends since it's a popular chain that fills up fast, and choose the Junior Suite if you're travelling as a small family.

faqTitle: FAQ — Questions travellers often ask about hotels in Phrae

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best Phrae hotel with great vibes?
faq.a: It depends on your travel style. By real review score, Hug Inn Phrae at 9.2 is the highest in the article, a boutique B&B in the old town, walk to markets and temples. If you want a garden hotel with a pool and good service, PhoomThai Garden Hotel scores 8.1 from over 1,000 reviews. If you like cool riverside design, Come Moon Loft, or teak woodwork, Baan I Inspire at 8.9. And on a budget, B2 Phrae from ฿590 is the best value.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Phrae hotels cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at about ฿590–1,015 per night. The most budget-friendly are B2 Phrae from ฿590, and Come Moon Loft and Taris Art from ฿650. The mid-range are Must Come ฿700, Phrae Nakara ฿750, Maeyom Palace ฿800, Huern Na Na ฿890, and PhoomThai and Hug Inn ฿900. Baan I Inspire starts at about ฿1,015 because of its design focus. All prices are approximate starting rates from standard rooms, and rates may be higher than usual during festivals.

faq.q: ❓ Which area should you stay in, in Phrae?
faq.a: Nai Wiang (the old town) suits anyone wanting to explore Khum Chao Luang, Baan Wongburi, temples, and markets on foot — Hug Inn, PhoomThai, Huern Na Na, Phrae Nakara, Taris Art, Baan I Inspire. Yom Riverside is quiet and near the walking street — Come Moon Loft. Across from the bus terminal is handy for coach arrivals — Maeyom Palace. Pa Maet / edge of town is easy to drive and light on the wallet — B2 Phrae.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Phrae · do you need your own car?
faq.a: There are three ways to reach Phrae: by air, landing at Phrae Airport (PRH) about 5–10 min from town, with flights from Bangkok; by coach, arriving at the provincial bus terminal near the city centre; or by car, about 6–7 hours from Bangkok, about 3 hours from Chiang Mai. In town the sights cluster in the old quarter, walkable or by bike, so if you stay in Nai Wiang you don't need a car, but if you stay on the edge of town like B2, or want to visit several spots outside town, a car is more flexible. Many hotels have free bikes and airport/bus-terminal transfers.

faq.q: ❓ Which Phrae hotels have a pool?
faq.a: In this article, the ones with a pool are Huern Na Na Boutique Hotel (outdoor saltwater pool), PhoomThai Garden Hotel (a pool in the garden with a spa and sauna), and Maeyom Palace Hotel (a large hotel with a pool). The small boutiques like Hug Inn, Come Moon Loft, and Must Come, and the budget options like Taris Art and B2 Phrae, have no pool — they focus on location and value instead.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book a Phrae hotel?
faq.a: Many of Phrae's great-vibe stays are small boutiques (Hug Inn 12 rooms, Come Moon Loft 15 rooms, Must Come about 20 rooms), so they fill up fast. Over long weekends, festivals, and the late-year travel season, book several weeks to a month ahead, especially Hug Inn, which fills up fastest. In normal periods 1–2 weeks is enough. Every platform usually offers Free Cancellation — we recommend locking in a rate like that first if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
